focus: First-order RC low-pass filter: frequency response H(jw) = 1 / (1 + j w R C). Let the learner change R, C and the input frequency. Show the cutoff frequency f_c = 1/(2 pi R C), the gain magnitude |H| in linear units and in dB, and the phase. Plot the magnitude response versus frequency with the current frequency marked. Guide them through the cutoff point (gain 1/sqrt(2), about -3 dB, phase -45 degrees) and a frequency ten times higher. Check that |H| = 1/sqrt(2) at f = f_c and that |H| tends to 1 as f tends to 0.
audience: Second-year electrical engineering undergraduates who know complex numbers and Ohm's law.
title: Signals and Systems lecture notes: first-order systems
excerpt: (paraphrased lecture notes on first-order systems) A resistor R in series with a capacitor C, with the output taken across the capacitor, forms a first-order low-pass filter. For a sinusoidal input at angular frequency w = 2 pi f, the capacitor has impedance 1/(j w C), so by voltage division the frequency response is H(jw) = Vout/Vin = 1 / (1 + j w R C). The product tau = R C is the time constant of the circuit. The magnitude is |H(jw)| = 1 / sqrt(1 + (w R C)^2) and the phase is angle H(jw) = -arctan(w R C). At low frequencies (w R C << 1) the output nearly equals the input; at high frequencies (w R C >> 1) the magnitude falls off approximately as 1/(w R C), i.e. by about 20 dB per decade. The corner (cutoff) frequency is w_c = 1/(R C), i.e. f_c = 1/(2 pi R C); there the magnitude is 1/sqrt(2) (about -3 dB) and the phase is -45 degrees. Magnitude in decibels is 20 log10 |H|.
